Serving as Lebanon's prime minister across three separate terms since 2005, this politician lost his final bid for a fourth term in January 2025 to the ICJ president, 9 votes to 84 — who is he?
Najib Mikati: Prime Minister of Lebanon (born 1955)
A journalist who once served a year in prison for defamation, this politician has served as Armenia's prime minister since 2018 while pushing for closer ties with Turkey — who is he?
Nikol Pashinyan: Prime Minister of Armenia since 2018. Nikol Vovayi Pashinyan (born 1 June 1975) is an Armenian politician who is serving as the 16th and current prime minister of Armenia since 2018.
Spelling out as Na-Ma-Shi-Va-Ya, this five-syllable Hindu mantra is the most important in Shaivism and offers salutations to 'the auspicious one' — what is it?
Om Namah Shivaya: Hindu mantra. Om Namah Shivaya (Devanagari: ॐ नमः शिवाय; IAST: Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya) is one of the most popular Hindu mantras and the most important mantra in Shaivism.
Known as 'Mr. Titanic' for his deep-sea expertise, this French explorer was among the five people killed when a submersible imploded near the famous wreck in June 2023 — who was he?
Paul-Henri Nargeolet: French naval officer and explorer (1946–2023)
Leader of Canada's Conservative Party and Official Opposition since 2022, this MP previously worked for Canadian Alliance leader Stockwell Day — who is he?
Nicknamed the 'Black Baron,' this scion of a Baltic German noble family became the last commander-in-chief of the White forces in southern Russia during the Civil War — who was he?
This Oglala Lakota leader won the war that bears his name, making the Lakota the only nation to defeat the U.S. on American soil — who was he?
Red Cloud: Leader of the Oglala Lakota (1822–1909)
Elected in January 2022 after the sudden death of her predecessor, this Maltese politician became the youngest-ever, and first Maltese, president of a major European institution — who is she?
Roberta Metsola: President of the European Parliament since 2022.

Held on March 17, the traditional death date of the foremost patron saint of Ireland, this religious and cultural holiday was made an official Christian feast day in the early 17th century. What day is it?
Signs of the coming of Judgement Day

Saint Patrick's Day: Cultural and religious celebration on 17 March. The day commemorates Saint Patrick and the arrival of Christianity in Ireland, and, by extension, celebrates the heritage and culture of the Irish in general.

Sparked partly by the Witwatersrand Gold Rush and the disenfranchised 'Uitlanders,' this turn-of-the-century conflict saw British garrisons besieged at Ladysmith, Mafeking, and Kimberley — which conflict?
Second Boer War: 1899–1902 war in South Africa.
Serving as Japan's prime minister through most of the postwar occupation, this diplomat forged close ties with the United States and once served as ambassador to Italy — who is he?
Shigeru Yoshida: Prime Minister of Japan (1946–1947; 1948–1954)
Born in a village near Vicenza, Italy, this longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress took the helm seven years after her husband Rajiv's assassination — who is she?
Commonly called "SBY," this retired general was only the second military man after Suharto to become Indonesia's president, serving two terms from 2004 — who is he?

Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono: President of Indonesia from 2004 to 2014. Yudhoyono won the 2004 presidential election—the first direct presidential election in Indonesia, defeating incumbent President Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Known by a name meaning 'behind the pool' after the palace where he resided, this monarch ruled the Ayutthaya Kingdom from 1709 to 1733 as the third ruler of the Ban Phlu Luang dynasty — who is he?
Thai Sa: King of Ayutthaya. The name "Thai Sa" (lit. "behind the pool") refers to the Banyongrattanat Palace, which was located by a pool where he often resided.
Author of the Port Huron Statement and one of the 'Chicago Seven' defendants, this 1960s New Left activist later served in the California legislature and was once married to Jane Fonda — who is he?
Born in the Ukrainian SSR, this politician served as Russia's ambassador to Malta and Greece before becoming Governor of Saint Petersburg and eventually chairing the Federation Council — who is she?
A key figure of Chile's Nueva Canción movement, this singer-songwriter was arrested and killed in the days following the 1973 coup that overthrew President Allende — who was he?
Víctor Jara: Chilean folk singer and activist (1932–1973)

Serving four non-consecutive terms as British Prime Minister between 1868 and 1894 — more than anyone else — this Liverpool-born statesman began as a Conservative MP before becoming the face of the Liberal Party — who was he?
Born in Georgia, this Red Army officer and engineer was the eldest son of a Bolshevik revolutionary who became head of the Soviet Union — who is he?
Yakov Dzhugashvili: Red Army officer and Joseph Stalin's son (1907–1943)
An early convert to Islam and a commander at the Battle of Badr in 624, this Arab Muslim general fought in the Ridda Wars and the early conquests of Persia, Syria and North Africa — who was he?
Zubayr ibn al-Awwam: Arab Muslim military commander (594–656)
Which of these people was born first?
Joan Clarke (born 1917) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was founded earliest?
SQL (founded 1974) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is a physicist?
Donna Strickland is a physicist. Donna Theo Strickland (born May 27, 1959) is a Canadian optical physicist and pioneer in the field of pulsed lasers.
Who among these is a chemist?
Stephanie Kwolek is a chemist. Stephanie Louise Kwolek (July 31, 1923 – June 18, 2014) was a Polish-American chemist known for inventing Kevlar (poly-paraphenylene terephthalamide).
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium: Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth: Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year was Harold Shipman born?
Harold Shipman: Harold Frederick Shipman (14 January 1946 – 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.
In what year was Fritz Haber born?
Fritz Haber: For this work, Haber has been called one of the most important scientists and industrial chemists in human history.
In what year was Ludwig Wittgenstein born?
Ludwig Wittgenstein: Wittgenstein was born in Vienna into one of Europe's richest families.
In what year did Lewis Carroll die?
Lewis Carroll: An avid puzzler, Carroll created the word ladder puzzle, which he called "Doublets", which was published in Vanity Fair magazine between 1879 and 1881.
In what year did Max Weber die?
Max Weber: Born in Erfurt in 1864, Weber studied law and history in Berlin, Göttingen, and Heidelberg.
In what year was Potassium discovered?
Potassium: Potassium is a chemical element; it has symbol K (from Neo-Latin kalium) and atomic number 19.
SEPECAT Jaguar: Breguet Aviation. As of 2026, the Jaguar remains in service with only the Indian Air Force.
Which country is Sukhoi Su-17 from?
Sukhoi Su-17: Soviet Union. The Sukhoi Su-17 (Russian: Су-17; NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
Sometimes called emotional blindness, this neuropsychological condition involves trouble identifying or describing one's own feelings, and appears in about half of autistic people. What is it?
Alexithymia (-), also called emotional blindness, is a neuropsychological phenomenon characterized by difficulties processing or describing one's emotions.
Dating back to the Neolithic Revolution around 13,000 BC, this branch of agriculture covers the breeding, feeding, and day-to-day care of livestock raised for meat, milk, or fiber — what's it called?
Animal husbandry is the branch of agriculture concerned with animals that are raised for meat, fibre, milk, or other products.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Found in almost every habitat except the open sea and the poles, the order Coleoptera is the largest of all and accounts for about a quarter of every known animal species — which insects are these?
Beetle are insects that form the order Coleoptera, in the superorder Holometabola.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
This large, stocky black corvid fills a niche across Eurasia comparable to a similar bird found in North America, but is bigger and huskier than its transatlantic counterpart — what species is it?
Carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Defined by a hollow dorsal nerve cord, an endostyle, and a post-anal tail at some point in life, this phylum spans vertebrates, tunicates, and lancelets alike — which option fits?
Chordate is a bilaterian animal belonging to the phylum Chordata (kor-).
This towering annual in the daisy family yields seeds in two flavors — oilseed (the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil) and the confectionary kind you crack as a snack — which plant?
Common sunflower (Helianthus annuus) is a large annual forb in the daisy family Asteraceae.
This bluish-purple discoloration of the skin, most visible on the lips, nail beds, and ear lobes, signals a drop in oxygen bound to hemoglobin in the blood — name the condition?
Cyanosis is the change of tissue color to a bluish-purple hue, as a result of decrease in the amount of oxygen bound to the hemoglobin in the red blood cells of the capillary bed.
Sucrose, lactose, and maltose are the best-known examples of this water-soluble carbohydrate class, each formed by linking two simple sugars together — what's the term?
Disaccharide (also called a double sugar or biose) is the sugar formed when two monosaccharides are joined by glycosidic linkage.
Once hunted nearly to extinction for lamp oil, these true seals of the genus Mirounga are named for the male's large trunk-like snout, with males weighing up to 4,000 kilograms — which animal?
Elephant seal are very large, oceangoing true seals in the genus Mirounga.
Aerobic exercise, laughter, dancing, and romantic love can all induce this intense feeling of well-being — which is also, less happily, a symptom of mania — what state is it?
Euphoria (yoo-) is the experience (or affect) of pleasure or excitement and intense feelings of well-being and happiness.
This omnivorous insect, common in North American homes, gets its name from ear-shaped hindwings and carries pincers on its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia is a species complex comprising the common earwig.
Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater has a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth and a pot-shaped bulb on the males' noses — what is it?
Gharial (Gavialis gangeticus), also known as gavial or fish-eating crocodile, is a crocodilian in the family Gavialidae and among the longest of all living crocodilians.

Caused by a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens, this non-cancerous condition results in enlarged breast tissue in men and can occur in newborns, adolescents, and older or obese men — name the condition?

Gynecomastia (also spelled gynaecomastia) is the non-cancerous enlargement of one or both breasts in men due to the growth of breast tissue as a result of a hormone imbalance between estrogens and androgens.

First described by an English physician in 1832, this cancer of the lymphocytes is identified by giant multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells in the lymph nodes, and about half its cases trace back to the Epstein-Barr virus. What is it?
Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a cancer where multinucleated Reed-Sternberg cells (RS cells) are present in the lymph nodes.
First used ritually by forager tribes in Central Africa and later adopted by Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this psychoactive plant alkaloid interacts with both opioid and serotonin receptors — what is it?
Ibogaine is a psychoactive indole alkaloid derived from plants such as Tabernanthe iboga, characterized by hallucinogenic and oneirogenic effects.

This American economist gave his name to a model for censored dependent variables — the 'tobit' — and advised the Council of Economic Advisers while championing government action to head off recessions. Who was he?

James Tobin (March 5, 1918 - March 11, 2002) was an American economist who served on the Council of Economic Advisers and consulted with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and taught at Yale University.

The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, this astronaut and aerospace engineer first studied in India before earning advanced degrees in the US and flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 — who was she?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 - February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.

Amphoteric and unreactive, this post-transition metal reacts with both acids and bases, melts at a low temperature, and tarnishes from shiny to dull gray in air — and three of its isotopes end major nuclear decay chains. Which element is it?
Lead is a chemical element with the symbol Pb (from the Latin plumbum) and atomic number 82.

Featuring a distinctive twin-boom design with a central pod housing the cockpit and guns, this American World War II fighter aircraft also served as a night fighter and long-range escort when fitted with drop tanks — which aircraft?
Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II.
A sugar alcohol used both as a low-calorie sweetener and as a medication to reduce eye and brain pressure. It's poorly absorbed by the intestines. What's the name of this compound?
Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication. It is unclear if use is safe in pregnancy.
Named in 1925 as an abbreviation of its chemical structure, this essential amino acid is required to kick-start protein synthesis — which amino acid is this?
Methionine (symbol Met or M) is an essential amino acid in humans.
These small, non-vascular, flowerless plants form dense green clumps or mats in damp, shady spots — name this group of plants?
Moss are small, non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division Bryophyta sensu stricto.
Found in tiny native amounts in Earth's crust but riding inside iron meteorites that never met oxygen, this hard, ductile metal shares its name with a small coin — which element is it?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.

Physicians in this medical specialty diagnose and surgically treat eye disorders — and can often spot signs of diseases elsewhere in the body just by examining a patient's eyes — what specialty is it?
Ophthalmology is the branch of medicine that deals with the diagnosis, treatment, and surgery of eye diseases and disorders.
This Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner coined the word 'conurbation' and his work contains one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally.' Who was he?
Patrick Geddes (2 October 1854 - 17 April 1932) was a Scottish biologist, sociologist, Comtean positivist, geographer, philanthropist and pioneering town planner.
This anxiety disorder involves an irrational, excessive, and persistent fear of a specific object or situation, often leading sufferers to go to great lengths to avoid it — what is it called?
Phobia is an anxiety disorder, defined by an irrational, unrealistic, persistent and excessive fear of an object or situation.
Ranging from linear chains to heavily branched polymers, these carbohydrate compounds — like starch, glycogen, and chitin — consist of many simple sugar units linked together. What are they called?
Polysaccharide (from Ancient Greek (pols) 'many, much' and (skkhar) 'sugar') are "compounds consisting of a large number of monosaccharides linked glycosidically".

Harvested from the seeds of several Plantago species, this common dietary fiber supplement relieves both constipation and mild diarrhea, and occasionally doubles as a food thickener — what is it called?
Psyllium is the common name used for several members of the plant genus Plantago whose seeds are used commercially for the production of mucilage.

This genus of roughly 60 herbaceous perennials in the buckwheat family includes the familiar pie vegetable prized for its tart stalks despite mildly toxic leaves — which genus, native to Europe and Asia?
Rheum (plant) is a genus of about 60 herbaceous perennial plants in the family Polygonaceae.
Which plant genus in the mint family, comprising nearly 1,000 species of shrubs and perennials, includes both a common cooking herb and — surprisingly — rosemary as one of its species?
Salvia is the largest genus of plants in the sage family Lamiaceae, with just under 1,000 species of shrubs, herbaceous perennials, and annuals.
Setting a world record for mental calculation at London's Imperial College in 1980, this self-taught Indian prodigy also wrote books on math, puzzles, and astrology — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi (4 November 1929 - 21 April 2013) was an Indian mental calculator, astrologer, and writer, popularly known as the "Human Computer".
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.
This Chinese physician and revolutionary led the 1911 Revolution, overthrew the Qing dynasty, and founded the Republic of China as its first president. Who was he?
Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 - 12 March 1925) was a Chinese physician, revolutionary and political philosopher who founded the Republic of China (ROC) and the Kuomintang (KMT).
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Latin for 'three-headed,' this large muscle on the back of the upper arm has three parts, one of which also crosses the shoulder joint — name the muscle?
Triceps (Latin for "three-headed muscle of the arm"), is a large muscle on the back of the upper limb of many vertebrates.
First glimpsed in 1892 through tobacco-plant disease and counted as the most numerous biological entity on Earth, this submicroscopic agent can only replicate inside a living cell. What is it?
Virus is a submicroscopic infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.

This unit of time is based on how long Earth takes to complete one full orbit around the Sun, with the precise scientific definition running about 365 days, 5 hours, and 48 minutes — what unit is this?

Year is a unit of time based on how long it takes the Earth to orbit the Sun. In scientific use, the tropical year (approximately 365 solar days, 5 hours, 48 minutes, 45 seconds) and the sidereal year (about 20 minutes longer) are more exact.
Also called sweet flag, this wetland plant contains psychoactive compounds and has been banned from American food products despite centuries of use in traditional medicine — which species?
Acorus calamus: Species of plant. Acorus calamus (also called sweet flag, sway or muskrat root, among many other common names) is a species of flowering plant with psychoactive chemicals.
This congenital condition causes a total or partial absence of pigment, leading to white hair, pale skin, and often pink or reddish eyes — what is it called?
Albinism: Disorder causing lack of pigmentation.
Native to North America but now invasive across Europe after being introduced, this semiaquatic mustelid preys on rodents, fish, and frogs — which animal?
American mink: Semiaquatic species of mustelid. Because of range expansion, the American mink is classed as a least-concern species by the IUCN.
Evolved from vespoid wasp ancestors in the Cretaceous, these insects are easily spotted by their elbowed antennae and slender, node-waisted bodies — what are they?
Ant: Family of insects. Nearly all ant colonies also have some fertile males called "drones" and one or more fertile females called "queens" (gynes).
Caused by excessive exposure to silver dust or compounds, this condition turns the skin a striking blue or blue-gray shade, especially in sun-exposed areas — what's it called?
Argyria: Medical condition. The most dramatic symptom of argyria is that the skin turns blue or blue-gray, and is usually most prominent in sun-exposed areas of the skin.
This broad category of technology uses machines and predetermined rules to reduce the need for human intervention in factories, boilers, and telephone switching — what is it?
Automation: Use of various control systems for operating equipment.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.
This medium-sized antelope of India and Nepal sports corkscrew horns up to 30 inches long and a striking two-tone coat, with white around the eyes set against black face stripes — which animal?
Blackbuck: Antelope native to India and Nepal. The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal.
Nicknamed 'murderer's thumb' or 'stubbed thumb,' this genetic trait gives about 2% of people a short, rounded thumb linked to the HOXD13 gene — what is it?
Brachydactyly type D: Abnormal shortening of the distal part of the thumb.
Alongside HTML and JavaScript, which style sheet language handles the layout, colors, and fonts of a webpage — separating presentation from content?
CSS: Style sheet language. CSS is a cornerstone technology of the World Wide Web, alongside HTML and JavaScript.

Time called her the "literary godmother" to Paris's Lost Generation, and her Black Sun Press printed early Hemingway and Henry Miller — but she also patented the first successful modern bra. Who was she?
Usually arising from damage to the developing brain before birth, this group of childhood movement disorders causes stiff or weak muscles, tremors, and poor coordination — what condition?
Cerebral palsy: Movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)

This ancient insect order traces back to the Late Jurassic, with chewing-mouthpart ancestors called "roachoids" scuttling around some 320 million years ago — yet only about 30 of its 4,600 species ever moved in with us. Which creature is it?
Cockroach: Insects of the order Blattodea.

Used in Chinese medicine for over 1,500 years, this genus of parasitic fungi infects insects and other arthropods, taking its name from Greek and Latin words meaning 'club' and 'head' — which genus is it?
Cordyceps: Genus of fungi. Cordyceps is a genus of ascomycete fungi (sac fungi) that includes over 260 species worldwide, many of which are parasitic.

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
This autoimmune disease attacks both the skin and skeletal muscles, causing a rash alongside worsening weakness, and is often linked to distinct myositis-specific autoantibodies — which condition?
Dermatomyositis: Autoimmune disease of skin and muscle. Dermatomyositis (DM) is a group of sytemic autoimmune inflammatory diseases primarily affecting the skin and skeletal muscles.
Developed as a 14-bed sleeper upgrade of an earlier airliner, which low-wing propeller monoplane cruised at 207 mph and reshaped air travel from the 1930s through World War II?
Douglas DC-3: Airliner and military transport aircraft family.

Defined by permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth and ranging from a 7-inch white-lipped snake to a nearly 19-foot king, which snake family includes most of the world's neck-flaring venomous serpents?
Elapidae: Family of venomous snakes. The family includes 55 genera with around 360 species and over 170 subspecies.

This Irish experimental physicist shared the 1951 Nobel with John Cockcroft for splitting the atom — the first nuclear transmutation, as the prize committee put it, "entirely under human control." Who was he?
Introduced to North America as early as 1840, this large eusocial wasp builds paper-like nests and preys on beetles, other wasps, and dragonflies — which insect is it?
European hornet: Species of wasp. The European hornet (Vespa crabro) is the largest eusocial wasp native to Europe.
Native to the Mediterranean and grown since ancient times, this teardrop-shaped fruit is technically a syconium and comes from the type species of a genus with over 800 members — what fruit is it?
Fig: Species of flowering plant, or its fruit.
This British-American theoretical physicist lent his name to a hypothetical genetically engineered 'tree' and a transform used in additive number theory — who was he?
Freeman Dyson: British theoretical physicist and mathematician (1923–2020)
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.
Spread mainly through blood-to-blood contact, this viral infection becomes chronic in about 70 percent of those first infected and can lead to liver failure over decades — which disease?
Hepatitis C: Human viral infection. Hepatitis C is an infectious disease caused by the hepatitis C virus (HCV) that primarily affects the liver; it is a type of viral hepatitis.

This field, drawing on sociology, anthropology, economics, and environmental science, studies how communities interact with their habitats — from urban sprawl to cultural and economic patterns across space — which discipline?
Human geography: Study of cultures, communities, people, lifestyle, and activities of people of the world.

Named from the Greek word for "fish" because of its dry, scaly skin, this family of genetic skin disorders ranges from a mild type mistaken for ordinary dry skin to a rare, life-threatening form — which condition?
Ichthyosis: Family of disorders causing dry, thickened, scaly skin.

Native to the Americas but now grown worldwide, one species of this flowering plant genus has become such a popular ornamental that it's classified as an invasive weed on four continents — which genus?
Jacaranda: Genus of trees. The generic name is also used as the common name.

The id Software programmer behind Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, and Quake later left to become CTO of Oculus VR — before walking away again to chase artificial general intelligence. Which 3D-graphics wizard is he?
John Carmack: American computer programmer and video game developer (born 1970)
Marketed as Nizoral, this antifungal medication also treats Cushing's syndrome and excess hair growth in women, though oral use risks liver damage — which drug?
This reddish-brown, bitter tincture dissolved opium poppy extract in alcohol and was once sold without a prescription as a cough and pain remedy — what is it?
Laudanum: Tincture of opium. Laudanum is a tincture of opium containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight (the equivalent of 1% morphine).
Native to the Indo-Pacific, this venomous aquarium favorite sports red-and-black banded warning colors and ostentatious spiny fins, and has become an invasive nightmare in the Caribbean — what is it?
This flowering legume genus boasts over 199 species and has become such a successful invasive spreader in Iceland that it's now considered an ecological problem — which genus?
Dubbed "sea locusts" by the ancient Assyrians and "prawn killers" by others, these burrow-dwelling crustaceans are among the most important predators of shallow tropical seas. What are they?
Mantis shrimp: Order of crustaceans. Mantis shrimp are carnivorous marine crustaceans of the order Stomatopoda (from Ancient Greek στόμα (stóma) 'mouth' and πούς (poús) 'foot').

Element 101, first made in 1955 by bombarding einsteinium with alpha particles, was the first that couldn't be produced by simply neutron-blasting a lighter element — and it honors the father of the periodic table. Which element is it?
Mendelevium: Chemical element with atomic number 101 (Md)
A self-taught Soviet tinkerer who later became a lieutenant general, he designed a famously reliable assault rifle but felt sorrow at how widely it spread — who was he?

The tallest and heaviest living species of deer, this Northern Hemisphere giant is topped in North American body mass only by the bison, and its males sport broad, hand-shaped antlers unlike any other deer's pointed racks. What is it?
Moose: Largest species of deer. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, land animal in North America, falling short only to the American bison in body mass.
The only mammal that's essentially cold-blooded, this burrowing "sand puppy" of the Horn of Africa also lives in an insect-like colony with a single breeding queen — what creature is it?
This reddish-brown, poisonous gas (formula NO2) is a key step in making nitric acid for fertilizer — and your gas stove quietly produces it while you cook. What is it?
Sold under the brand name Prilosec, this proton-pump inhibitor treats acid reflux and peptic ulcers — what is it?
Omeprazole: Medication to treat gastroesophageal reflux disease and other conditions.
Located behind the stomach, this gland is 99 percent exocrine yet still secretes insulin and glucagon to regulate blood sugar — which organ?
Pancreas: Organ of the digestive system and endocrine system of vertebrates.

Famous for the giant throat pouch beneath its long beak, this large water bird's eight living species range from the tropics to temperate zones, with some even flying inland to Australia's Red Centre after heavy rains — what bird is this?
Pelican: Genus of large water birds with a throat pouch.
This toxic gas, which smells like freshly cut hay, was responsible for tens of thousands of deaths as a chemical weapon in World War I — what is it?
Named after the American diplomat who introduced it from Mexico, this red-and-green Christmas plant is not actually toxic to pets — which plant?
Also known as face blindness, this cognitive disorder leaves a person unable to recognize familiar faces — even their own — while other visual skills stay intact. What is it?
